clinical_matches.notable_studies: The major cold-literature synthesis remains Hemila and Chalker (PMID 23440782), which found shorter cold duration but limited prevention in the general population. Later review updates include PMID 38082300, while high-exertion prevention effects were highlighted in earlier analyses such as PMID 17636648.
clinical_matches.notes: Vitamin C clearly supports deficiency correction, antioxidant biology, and collagen synthesis. For common-cold outcomes, the best human evidence supports modest shortening of duration rather than strong prevention effects in the general population.

clinical_matches.effect_direction_rationale: Reference-only NIH ODS fact sheet; study_type=reference; evidence_level=reference; no PMID/NCT/DOI-backed standalone manganese clinical evidence identified.
clinical_matches.notable_studies: NIH ODS Manganese anchors the evidence around enzyme-cofactor biology, dietary adequacy, and toxicity risk from excessive exposure. Because stand-alone manganese supplementation trials with clear clinical endpoints remain sparse, this entry should stay conservative and deficiency-oriented rather than claim broad therapeutic efficacy.
clinical_matches.notes: Human supplementation evidence for manganese is limited. NIH ODS mainly supports manganese as an essential trace-element cofactor, while direct interventional outcome data are sparse and usually embedded in multimineral or deficiency-related contexts rather than stand-alone manganese efficacy trials.

ingredients.name: Manganese
ingredients.notes: An inorganic salt form with lower absorption than organic chelates. More likely to cause GI upset at higher doses. Inexpensive, so it's common in budget multivitamins. If your label says sulfate, you're getting a basic form. B28 audit 2026-04-25: Mn class-equivalence (inherent low F).

condition_hits.action: Avoid manganese supplementation above 5 mg/day in liver disease. In advanced cirrhosis or liver failure, avoid supplemental manganese entirely. Evaluate manganese status if neurological symptoms develop.
condition_hits.alert_body: Manganese clearance can be impaired in liver disease, leading to accumulation. If you have liver disease, avoid high-dose manganese unless your clinician monitors levels.
condition_hits.alert_headline: Manganese clearance depends on the liver
condition_hits.informational_note: Manganese depends on liver clearance — relevant to people with liver conditions.
condition_hits.mechanism: Manganese is excreted almost exclusively via bile. Liver disease impairs biliary excretion, leading to systemic accumulation. Excess manganese deposits in the basal ganglia (globus pallidus), producing manganism — a Parkinson-like neurotoxic syndrome with rigidity, bradykinesia, and psychiatric symptoms. MRI T1 hyperintensity in liver disease patients with elevated manganese is well-documented.
